subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should this be fixed first by making CLI observers RPC-first/no-maintenance while a gateway owns the DB, by adding a single-writer lease, or by prioritizing malformed-DB quarantine and recovery?
rationale: The source boundary is clear, but the permanent fix changes CLI observability, doctor/migration behavior, gateway ownership, and data recovery for persisted shared state.

options.title: RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Health/status/stability prefer the running gateway and permit only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file access while a gateway lease is active.

options.title: Single-writer lease first
options.body: The gateway owns write and WAL-maintenance access through an explicit lease, and other processes refuse writer-style shared DB opens while it is held.

options.title: Recovery/quarantine first
options.body: Malformed shared DBs are preserved and quarantined before prevention work, reducing post-corruption damage while leaving the concurrent-opener class for follow-up.

recommendation.title: RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Health/status/stability prefer the running gateway and permit only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file access while a gateway lease is active.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared SQLite state database introduction and the broadest affected-path history point to steipete for the DB ownership/recovery contract decision.
